key_insight: Autocata turns catalyst screening into an autonomous, language-driven workflow by encoding reaction-network expertise into reusable capabilities that can generate, filter, and rank candidate catalyst structures.
engineering_relevance: This lowers the human overhead in complex catalyst discovery campaigns and provides a scalable software architecture for self-driving materials research across multi-step reaction pathways.
method: Pretrains a Transformer on 2 million catalyst-adsorbate structures to learn surface chemistry representations.
Uses a registry of 79 adsorbate-specialized generative models covering C, N, O, and H reaction intermediates.
Decomposes natural-language goals into workflow steps, then configures generators, validates structures, and runs ML-potential evaluations with adaptive re-routing when needed.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports demonstrations on CH4 activation, nitrogen reduction, and CO2-to-methanol pathways, showing the agent can execute across distinct catalytic task families.
watch_item: Performance likely depends on the completeness of the capability registry and the reliability of physical/geometric filtering when the workflow encounters unseen reaction steps.
paper_title: Autocata: Reaction-network-guided autonomous catalyst screening via capability-centric AI
